moves.missing: (iii) flag missing items against a checklist

provenance: The playbook was substantially model-generated by a senior partner, not written from observed practice. Agreement with the corpus is evidence that two syntheses agree, not that either is right.

prompts.title: Summarize a Corporate Organizational Document
fields: Entity type, state of formation, and date of formation/incorporation
Authorized and outstanding capital structure (classes of stock or membership interests, voting rights, liquidation preferences, anti-dilution provisions)
Governance structure: board composition, quorum and voting requirements, reserved matters requiring supermajority or minority approval
Restrictions on transfer of equity interests (right of first refusal, right of first offer, drag-along, tag-along, co-sale rights)
Change-of-control provisions: consent requirements, deemed liquidation events
Any unusual or non-standard provisions Flag any provisions that would require third-party consent or stockholder approval in connection with the proposed acquisition
prompts.when_to_use: Use when reviewing corporate governance documents for a target entity to build the corporate diligence section of the due diligence memo and to identify approval requirements for the transaction.

prompts.title: Identify Key Corporate Diligence Risks Across the Entity Structure
fields: Identify all material risks or issues from a buyer's perspective, including: a. Third-party consent requirements for the proposed transaction b. Minority interests that could block or complicate the transaction c. Anti-assignment or change-of-control provisions in the organizational documents d. Pre-emptive rights or rights of first refusal that must be waived before closing e. Governance provisions inconsistent with buyer's post-closing operating model
Rate each risk as High, Medium, or Low based on likelihood of impact on the transaction

For each High-rated risk, suggest a mitigation approach (e.g., obtain consent, amend document at closing, structure around). Please present findings in a risk register format: Risk | Description | Rating | Mitigation
prompts.when_to_use: Use after completing the initial corporate document review to compile the corporate diligence findings for the deal team and for inclusion in the due diligence memo.

prompts.title: Flag Missing Corporate Diligence Items Against Checklist
fields: Identify every item on the corporate checklist that has not been produced in the data room

For each missing item, indicate whether the absence is: (a) a material gap requiring immediate follow-up, (b) a secondary item that can be requested in a follow-up round, or (c) potentially not applicable to this target

Draft a follow-up information request for the missing material items, formatted as a numbered list ready to send to target's counsel. Key items to prioritize: good standing certificates for all entities, evidence of authorization for the transaction, minute books and board resolutions for the past three years, list of all subsidiaries and joint ventures, and current capitalization table certified by the secretary
prompts.when_to_use: Use mid-diligence to identify and chase outstanding corporate items before the due diligence period closes.

prompts.title: Synthesize Corporate Diligence Findings Across All Entity Documents
fields: Describe the target's corporate structure (number and type of entities, jurisdiction of organization, ownership chain)
Summarize the capital structure of the parent, including all classes of equity, option pools, and any convertible instruments
Set out all material issues identified during the review in order of significance
Identify all third-party consents and stockholder approvals required to consummate the transaction

List all open items (documents not yet produced or issues not yet resolved) Write in formal legal memo style. Use present tense. Do not include recommendations — those will go in the risk summary section of the memo
prompts.when_to_use: Use to compile the final corporate diligence section of the due diligence memo after all documents have been reviewed and individual workstream summaries have been prepared.

prompts.title: Summarize a Material Contract
fields: Parties and effective date
Subject matter and scope of the arrangement
Term and renewal provisions
Financial terms (fees, payment schedule, revenue commitment, minimum purchase obligations)
Exclusivity provisions (if any)
Change-of-control clause: does the counterparty have consent rights, termination rights, or repricing rights triggered by the acquisition?
Assignment restrictions
Termination rights (for cause, for convenience, upon change of control, upon insolvency)
Representations and warranties; indemnification provisions
Limitation of liability and liability cap
Governing law and dispute resolution Flag any provisions that create risk for a buyer or that may require negotiation or consent in connection with the acquisition
prompts.when_to_use: Use for each material contract in the data room to build a systematic contract diligence database and to identify consent and assignment issues before signing.

prompts.title: Identify Key Risks Across the Contracts Portfolio and Flag Change-of-Control
fields: Critical (contract is material to the business and counterparty has termination right)
High (contract is material and consent is required but termination is not automatic)

Medium (contract is non-material or provision is unlikely to be exercised) 4. Recommend which consents should be obtained as a pre-closing covenant and which should be covered by a rep and warranty in the purchase agreement. Please present the output as a change-of-control consent tracker table
prompts.when_to_use: Use to identify and track all contracts requiring third-party consent as a condition to closing or as a pre-closing deliverable — one of the most critical workstreams in any M&A transaction.

prompts.title: Flag Missing Contracts and Synthesize Contracts Diligence Findings
fields: Overview of the target's material contracts (number, categories, aggregate value)
Summary of key commercial terms across the portfolio (average contract term, payment terms, termination provisions)
All material issues identified (change-of-control provisions, concentration risk, unusual terms, missing contracts)
Open items and recommended follow-up Write in formal legal memo style
prompts.when_to_use: Use at the conclusion of the contracts diligence workstream to compile all findings into the definitive contracts section of the due diligence memo.

prompts.title: Summarize an IP Assignment Agreement and Assess IP Ownership Chain
fields: Summarize each document's key terms, including the scope of the IP assigned or licensed, any retained rights, field-of-use restrictions, and sublicensing rights

Assess whether the target's core IP (software code, patents, trade secrets, brand) appears to be fully owned by the company or whether there are gaps in the ownership chain (e.g., contractors who did not sign IP assignments, jointly invented patents, licensed-in technology embedded in the product)
Identify any open-source software licenses disclosed in the data room and flag any licenses (GPL, AGPL, LGPL) that could impose copyleft obligations affecting the product

List all third-party IP licenses that are material to the business and flag any that contain change-of-control or assignment restrictions. Flag any IP ownership gaps that require remediation before signing
prompts.when_to_use: Use for technology company targets where IP is a primary asset being acquired and where IP ownership chain integrity is a critical diligence concern.

prompts.title: Identify Key IP Risks and Synthesize IP Diligence Findings
fields: Ownership gaps or defects in the IP chain of title
IP licensed in on terms that restrict commercialization or change of control
Open-source license compliance issues (actual or potential copyleft contamination)
Unregistered trademarks or domain names that could be challenged post-closing
Pending or threatened IP infringement claims
Employee or contractor IP disputes

IP maintenance lapses (missed maintenance fees, lapsed registrations) Part B — Memo Section: Synthesize all findings into a formal IP diligence section for the due diligence memo. Include a summary IP schedule (list of all registered IP, applications, and material licenses)
prompts.when_to_use: Use at the conclusion of IP diligence to compile findings for the due diligence memo and to identify IP-specific reps and warranties that should be included in the purchase agreement.

prompts.title: Summarize Key Employment Agreements and Identify Retention and Change-of-Control Issues
fields: Compensation: base salary, target bonus, equity holdings (vested and unvested), and any special compensation arrangements
Severance: severance entitlements on termination without cause, resignation for good reason, and double-trigger change-of-control

Restrictive Covenants: non-compete, non-solicitation of employees and customers, and non-disparagement provisions — include duration, geographic scope, and whether the covenant is likely enforceable under applicable law
Change-of-Control Provisions: accelerated vesting provisions (single-trigger vs. double-trigger), transaction bonuses, retention bonuses

Intellectual Property Assignments: confirm that the agreement contains a current, broadly-worded IP assignment clause After summarizing individual agreements, provide a comparison table showing key terms across all executives. Flag any provisions that create unusual retention risk or golden parachute payment obligations
prompts.when_to_use: Use early in diligence to identify retention and change-of-control payment risks and to inform the buyer's post-closing retention planning.

prompts.title: Flag Missing HR Diligence Items and Synthesize Employment Findings
fields: Wage and hour exposure (FLSA, state overtime, independent contractor misclassification)
Benefit plan compliance issues (401(k) plan loans, ACA compliance, pension underfunding)
WARN Act obligations on potential post-closing restructuring
Labor relations issues (union organizing, collective bargaining agreements)
Outstanding or threatened employment litigation Part C — Memo Synthesis: Draft the HR/employment section of the due diligence memo
prompts.when_to_use: Use at the conclusion of the employment diligence workstream to compile all findings and produce the HR section of the due diligence memo.

prompts.title: Summarize Real Estate Holdings and Identify Lease Issues
fields: Property type (office, warehouse, manufacturing, retail) and location
Owned vs. leased; if leased: landlord, commencement date, expiration date, renewal options, and annual rent
Square footage and permitted use
Change-of-control or assignment provisions: does the lease require landlord consent for the proposed acquisition?
Sublease rights and any existing subleases
Termination rights (landlord's or tenant's) and default provisions
Any ongoing landlord disputes, rent deferrals, or LOI for renewal Create a real estate summary table. Flag all leases requiring landlord consent as a closing deliverable
prompts.when_to_use: Use to build the real estate diligence database and to identify leases requiring consent — a commonly overlooked source of closing risk.

prompts.title: Summarize Pending Litigation and Regulatory Matters
fields: Case/matter name, court or agency, and date filed or initiated
Nature of the claim or proceeding (contract, tort, IP, employment, regulatory, environmental, criminal)
Amount in controversy or potential exposure (if quantified)
Current status and expected timeline to resolution
Any insurance coverage for the claim

Management's assessment of likelihood of adverse outcome and accrual status (per financial statements) After individual matter summaries, provide an aggregate exposure table and flag any matter where: (a) exposure is material relative to the purchase price, (b) the matter involves a government agency or potential criminal exposure, (c) the claim could survive closing as a liability of the buyer, or (d) the matter is not disclosed in the target's financial statements
prompts.when_to_use: Use to build the litigation section of the due diligence memo and to identify matters that should be covered by specific indemnities in the purchase agreement.

prompts.title: Identify Regulatory Compliance Risks and Flag Missing Compliance
fields: List all material permits, licenses, and regulatory approvals held by the target, including issuing authority, expiration date, and any conditions or restrictions
Identify any permits or approvals that are non-transferable or that require regulatory pre-approval for a change of control
Flag any compliance gaps: permits expired or approaching expiration, missing required certifications, disclosed regulatory investigations or notices of violation
Assess the risk that the proposed transaction structure (stock vs. asset deal) affects the transferability of key licenses

Flag any disclosed or apparent violations of applicable law that could result in regulatory action, fines, or reputational harm post-closing. Present findings as a regulatory risk register: Permit/Requirement | Status | Transferability | Risk Level | Recommended Action
prompts.when_to_use: Use for targets in regulated industries to identify licensing and compliance risks that could affect the buyer's ability to operate the business post-closing.

prompts.title: Synthesize Tax Diligence Findings and Flag Material Tax Risks
fields: Summarize the target's tax profile: entity classification, tax year, jurisdictions of filing, consolidated group membership (if any)
Identify any material open tax years or ongoing audits, and the potential exposure associated with each
Flag any tax positions that appear aggressive or that have not been disclosed to auditors
Assess sales tax nexus and compliance across the jurisdictions where the target has operations or sells products/services — flag any apparent nexus without registration
Note any deferred tax liabilities that are not reflected in the purchase price adjustment mechanism
Flag any net operating loss carryforwards (NOLs), noting any Section 382 limitations on their use post-acquisition

Identify any tax risks specific to the proposed transaction structure (e.g., Section 338(h)(10) election feasibility, built-in gains, transfer taxes). Summarize findings in a tax risk register and draft the tax section of the due diligence memo
prompts.when_to_use: Use at the conclusion of the tax diligence workstream to compile findings for the due diligence memo and to brief the tax practice group on issues requiring specialist analysis.

prompts.title: Summarize Financial Statements and Flag Accounting and Finance Risks
fields: Risk Description: concise description of the issue (1-3 sentences)
Workstream: which diligence workstream identified this risk
Risk Rating: High / Medium / Low (based on combination of probability and magnitude of impact)
Financial Exposure: estimated dollar exposure range, if quantifiable

Recommended Mitigation: one of the following — (i) specific rep and warranty in purchase agreement, (ii) pre-closing covenant, (iii) closing condition, (iv) specific indemnity / escrow holdback, (v) price adjustment, (vi) further diligence required, (vii) no action required

Status: Open / Resolved / Covered by Insurance (R&W insurance or other) Sort the risk matrix by Risk Rating (High first), then by Workstream. Present as a table. At the end of the table, provide a one-paragraph overall risk summary
Third-party consents required (by contract type and counterparty)
Regulatory approvals required
Pre-closing restructuring or remediation steps (e.g., IP assignments, entity clean-up)
Financial statement or certification deliverables
Key employee retention agreements to be executed before closing Format Part B as a checklist suitable for use as a closing checklist annex to the purchase agreement
prompts.when_to_use: Use to build the financial diligence section of the due diligence memo and to flag financial issues that should be reflected in the purchase price or purchase agreement representations.
